items.text: AMEND (T) AND RECOMMIT TO CONSUMER PROTECTION
COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the general business law, in relation to prohibiting the sale of drop-side cribs
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6356

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the general business law, in relation to prohibiting
the sale of drop-side cribs


 PURPOSE :
To prohibit the import, manufacture, sale and distribution of
drop-side cribs in the State of New York.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Section 1 - Legislative Intent

Section 2 - The General Business Law is amended by adding a new
section 399-i to prohibit the import, manufacture, sale, hold or offer
for sale or distribution of drop-side cribs in NYS; set forth
applicable definitions; authorize enforcement powers and procedures of
the NYS Attorney General in terms of violations; and create a civil
penalty structure for violations.

Section 3 - Sets for the effective date.

 EXISTING LAW :
There is no current statewide law banning the sale of drop-side cribs
in the State of New York.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Despite nationwide attention surrounding the deaths of eleven babies
as a result of the dangers associated with drop-side cribs, they are
still being sold in the marketplace as a safe and suitable sleeping
environment for infants, babies and toddlers. Even the new head of the
Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) has stated that the Agency
"hasn't been acting as quickly as it should" on crib safety problems.
Therefore, New York State is being proactive and addressing this issue
now rather than waiting for possible new upcoming standards,
guidelines or worse yet, another child's death. It is important to
note that tragically two of the eleven deaths, reported by the CPSC,
occurred in the State of New York. One child died in the Bronx and the
other in the Gouverneur in St. Lawrence County.

According to the CPSC, due to the nature of the mechanisms of
drop-side cribs, the hardware can break or deform, causing the
drop-side to detach. When this occurs, a space is created between the
drop-side and the crib mattress. Infants and toddlers can easily roll
into this space and become entrapped which can lead to suffocation.
Other injuries associated with drop-side cribs include falls when the
side completely detaches which led to youngsters experiencing bumps,
bruises and concussions.

In addition, the ASTM Subcommittee on Full-Size Cribs has been
investigating incidents related to drop-sides on full-size cribs.
According to the ASTM, many of the incidents showed hardware failure
related to miss-assembly and re-assembly of the crib. This
subcommittee has been charged with consideration of revisions to the
standard that would eliminate such functional drop-sides, thereby
reducing the need for hardware assemblies and preventing any failures
related to the drop-sides on cribs.

Moreover, counties in New York State have already begun to ban the
sale of drop-side cribs.  Parents on Long Island who attribute their
infant sons' death to a defective drop-side crib have worked with the
county legislatures to ban the sale of these cribs in Suffolk and
Nassau counties.  Having one comprehensive statewide law will create a
consistent marketplace for consumers and stores which are preferable
to a number of local laws which may differ from locality to locality.
Therefore, this legislation would effectively prohibit the import,
manufacture, sale and distribution of drop-side cribs in New York
State.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
This is a new bill in 2009.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become a law.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the general business law, in relation to prohibiting the sale of unsafe cribs
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6356A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the general business law, in relation to prohibiting
the sale of unsafe cribs


 PURPOSE :

To prohibit the import, sale, manufacture, hold or offering for sale
or distribution of any cribs in New York State that would be deemed
"unsafe".

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section One - Legislative Intent.

Section Two - The General Business Law is amended to create a new
section 399-i to define the term "unsafe crib" as any crib that does
not conform to the standards endorsed or established by the federal
Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) and the standards endorsed
or established by the American Society for Testing and Materials
International (ASTM). Prohibits the import, manufacture, sale, hold or
offer for sale or distribution any cribs deemed "unsafe" in the State
of New York. Authorizes enforcement powers and procedures of the NYS
Attorney General as well as the creation of a civil penalty structure
for violations.

Section Three - Sets forth the effective date.

 EXISTING LAW :
There is no current state law that bans the sale of cribs in New York
State that do not meet the safety standards set forth in this
legislation.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Despite nationwide attention surrounding the deaths of twelve babies
as a result of the dangers posed by malfunctioning drop-side cribs,
they are still being sold in the marketplace as a safe and suitable
sleeping environment for infants, babies and toddlers. Even the new
Chair of the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) has stated that
the Agency "has not been acting as quickly as it should" on crib
safety problems. Therefore, New York State is being proactive and
addressing this issue now rather than waiting for possible new
upcoming standards, guidelines or worse yet, another child's death.
It is important to note that tragically two of the twelve deaths,
reported by the CPSC, occurred in the State of New York. One child
died in the Bronx and the other in Gouverneur, New York located in St.
Lawrence County.

According to the CPSC, due to the nature of the mechanisms of
drop-side cribs, the hardware can break or deform, causing the
drop-side to detach. When this occurs, a space is created between the
drop-side and the crib mattress. Infants and toddlers can easily roll
into this space and become entrapped which can lead to suffocation.
Other injuries associated with drop-side cribs include falls when the
side completely detaches which led to youngsters experiencing bumps,
bruises and concussions.

In addition, the American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM)
Subcommittee on Full-Size Cribs has been investigating incidents
related to drop-sides on full-size cribs. According to the ASTM, many
of the incidents showed hardware failure related to miss-assembly and
re-assembly of the crib. This subcommittee was charged with
consideration of revisions to the standard and chose to change the
standard to eliminate such functional sides. Elimination of a
drop-side on cribs reduces the need for hardware assemblies and
prevents such sides from malfunctioning or failing.

Moreover, counties in New York State have begun adopting laws that ban
the sale of drop-side cribs. Parents on Long Island who attribute the
death of their infant son to a defective drop-side crib worked with
the county legislatures in Suffolk and Nassau counties to enact a law.
Rockland County has also enacted its own law. It is preferable to have
one comprehensive statewide law, which will create a consistent
marketplace for consumers and retailers, than a number of local laws
that differ from locality to locality.

Therefore, this legislation provides that all cribs being sold,
distributed, imported, manufactured, held or offered for sale in the
State of New York must meet the standards endorsed or established by
the CPSC and ASTM for safety and structural integrity. This will
include not only the elimination of drop-sides but also specifications
concerning corner posts, slats, mattress support and others.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
This is a new bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become a law.
